fullPassage: The sit-in movement was part of the struggle for racial equality in the US. Its goal was to end the forced separation of races in public places. One of the most important events of this movement was the moment when some African American college students sat in a segregated section of a restaurant in North Carolina. They were told to leave, but they protested by remaining in their seats. This was not the first sit-in of the civil rights movement, but it led to a series of similar protests. During them, protesters occupied seats in places where races were segregated, including restaurants and libraries. They refused to move unless they were either served or arrested. Many establishments decided to end their practice of racial segregation rather than deal with more protests. These sit-ins helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which officially ended segregation in public places.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the practice of keeping people of different races or groups apart from each other"

det.korean: equality=평등 / protest=항의 / movement=운동 / segregation=(인종) 차별, 분리
det.analysis:
① equality(평등): 사람들을 동등하게 대하는 것으로 정의와 반대
② protest(항의): 반대 의사를 표현하는 것
③ movement(운동): 사회적 활동·운동
④ segregation(차별/분리): 다른 인종·집단을 서로 떼어놓는 관행 ←정답
det.tip: keeping different races apart(다른 인종을 떼어놓음) → segregation(차별/분리)

questions.passage: Many establishments decided to end their practice of racial segregation rather than deal with more protests. These sit-ins helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which __________ (official) ended segregation in public places.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: official(형용사: 공식적인) → officially(부사: 공식적으로). 동사 ended를 꾸미는 부사
det.analysis: official(형용사)을 부사 officially로 바꿔요. 뒤의 동사 ended(끝냈다)를 꾸미는 자리라 부사가 필요해요. 'officially ended(공식적으로 끝냈다)'가 맞아요
det.tip: 동사(ended)를 꾸미는 자리 = 부사. official + -ly → officially

questions.passage: The sit-in movement was part of the struggle for racial equality in the US. Its goal was to end the forced __________ (separate) of races in public places.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: separate(동사: 분리하다) → separation(명사: 분리). the ... of 구조에서 명사 자리
det.analysis: separate(동사)를 명사 separation으로 바꿔요. 'the forced ___ of races'에서 the와 of 사이 명사 자리라 명사가 필요해요. 'the forced separation of races(강요된 인종 분리)'가 맞아요
det.tip: the ___ of 구조 = 명사 자리. separate → separation(분리)

questions.passage: The sit-in movement was part of the struggle for racial equality in the US. Its goal was to end the forced separation of races in public places. One of the most important events of this movement was the moment when some African American college students sat in a segregated section of a restaurant in North Carolina. They were told to leave, but they protested by remaining in their seats. This was not the first sit-in of the civil rights movement, but it led to a series of __________. During them, protesters occupied seats in places where races were segregated, including restaurants and libraries. They refused to move unless they were either served or arrested. Many establishments decided to end their practice of racial segregation rather than deal with more protests. These sit-ins helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which officially ended segregation in public places.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: violent riots=폭력적 폭동 / similar protests=비슷한 시위 / legal battles=법적 다툼 / peaceful marches=평화 행진
det.analysis:
① violent riots(폭력적 폭동): 시위대는 자리에 조용히 남아 저항 → 폭력과 무관
② similar protests(비슷한 시위): 첫 연좌 농성이 '비슷한 시위'의 연속으로 이어졌고, 바로 뒤 문장이 그 시위들(자리 점거)을 설명 ←정답
③ legal battles(법적 다툼): 현장 연좌 농성이지 법정 다툼이 아님
④ peaceful marches(평화 행진): 행진이 아니라 앉아서 하는 연좌 농성(sit-in)
det.tip: a series of ___ + 뒤 문장이 유사한 연좌 시위 설명 → similar protests(비슷한 시위)

questions.passage: The sit-in movement was part of the struggle for racial equality in the US. Its goal was to end the forced separation of races in public places. One of the most important events of this movement was the moment when some African American college students sat in a segregated section of a restaurant in North Carolina. They were told to leave, but they protested by remaining in their seats. This was not the first sit-in of the civil rights movement, but it led to a series of similar protests. During them, protesters occupied seats in places where races were segregated, including restaurants and libraries. They refused to move unless they were either served or arrested. Many establishments decided to end their practice of racial segregation rather than deal with __________. These sit-ins helped pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which officially ended segregation in public places.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: more protests=더 많은 시위 / higher taxes=더 높은 세금 / legal fees=법적 비용 / angry owners=화난 주인
det.analysis:
① more protests(더 많은 시위): 기관들은 계속되는 시위를 감당하기보다 인종 차별을 끝내기로 함 → '더 많은 시위'를 다루는 것 대신 ←정답
② higher taxes(더 높은 세금): 세금은 글에 언급 없음
③ legal fees(법적 비용): 문맥 부적절
④ angry owners(화난 주인): 압박한 것은 시위대이지 주인이 아님
det.tip: end segregation rather than deal with ___ → more protests(더 많은 시위)
